operations.name: Vendor Supply – Near-Net Forging
operations.setup_note: Supplier matched dies form the lug contours, collar, journal transitions, relief and peripheral notches to the released forging/CAD definition. Supply the 100-piece order as trimmed, skin-cleaned, certified T6 preforms; this operation represents the purchased forging supply, not an additional charge on top of purchased blanks.

operations.name: Vendor Forging Integrity Gate
operations.setup_note: At the forging supplier, present cleaned preforms to the penetrant inspection station before release for machining. Apply the approved TM-2005 acceptance specification and retain lot traceability.

operations.name: Forging Flash Smooth and Clean
operations.setup_note: Support the received T6 forging in a soft bench nest and smooth residual trimmed flash without altering die-formed contours. Remove loose contamination before chucking and avoid notches or stress risers at blends.

operations.name: CNC Turn – First End
operations.setup_note: Hold the forged left lug in balanced contour soft jaws aligned to X, with non-marking travelling support where the unsupported span requires it. Skim the right end, establish journal datum C using light G71/G70 cuts, and finish the designated collar right-face land in the same spindle orientation.

operations.name: CNC Turn – Second End
operations.setup_note: Reverse the part into a protective split-sleeve fixture on finished datum C, using the first machined collar face as the axial pickup. Face the opposite end and collar land, then lightly skim and finish the collar OD while retaining the specified die-formed drafts, blends and relief.

operations.name: VMC – Gang Flats, Holes and Mounting Slot
operations.setup_note: Clamp datum C in a protective, positively clocked indexable fixture and retain that single clamping while indexing for opposing Y and Z access; use gang/straddle cutters for paired flats. Establish A first, pick up its finished plane, and establish B by drilling before finishing the left slot relative to A-B; machine both sides of each contact pad by indexed access.

operations.name: Final Deburr and Clean
operations.setup_note: Support the machined part in a soft nest and rapidly deburr hole exits, slot boundaries and remaining machined edges to the 0.5 mm maximum edge-break requirement. Clean chips from both mounting openings and contact faces without rounding datum surfaces.

operations.name: Final Shop-Floor Quality Gate
operations.setup_note: Present sampled parts to dedicated snap, plug and datum-specific functional gauges under the approved SPC plan. Check A-B mounting controls separately from C-referenced controls, with sampled flatness, collar perpendicularity, journal finish and visual blend/flash checks.

clarifications.question: Can you provide the released Revision B3 master CAD model?
Does Revision B3 retain the interpretation that the collar is 6.63 mm over the outer radii and 7.63 mm at its base?
clarifications.suggested_default: Use the supplied over-radii interpretation provisionally, but release collar machining only against confirmed Revision B3 geometry.

clarifications.question: Does the 12.15/11.85 mm feature F12 define the right lug's external thickness rather than an axial slot?
clarifications.suggested_default: Treat F12 as the right lug thickness and produce it by paired side milling; do not cut an additional axial slot.

clarifications.question: What is the specified axial extent of the diameter-70 relief F10?
clarifications.suggested_default: Use the released master CAD definition; do not infer a 5 mm axial width from radial depth or blend radius.

clarifications.question: Is qualified near-net forging tooling already available for this 100-piece order?
clarifications.suggested_default: Source an existing qualified supplier preform; if tooling is unavailable, quote its non-recurring cost separately without substituting solid bar.

clarifications.question: What pre-machining NDT acceptance specification applies to this forging under TM-2005?
clarifications.suggested_default: Retain supplier penetrant inspection before machining, with the acceptance specification approved before production.

assumptions.text: The forging material designation and organizational overrides require a purchased near-net forging, not envelope-sized bar. All stock dimensions and machining allowance remain null because the preform is defined by its forging drawing.

Supplier billet weighing/cutting, heating, press trimming and skin removal are upstream activities included in the purchased forging supply, not separately quoted shop operations. Supplier-certified T6 processing replaces the generic forging template's normalize/anneal step; no post-machining heat treatment is specified.

The supplier must certify the specified material condition and minimum yield requirement. Steel-specific forging temperatures, hot-trim temperatures and mandatory normalizing guidance are not applied to this aluminium preform.

The die supplies the rounded lug ends, large blends, drafts, diameter-70 relief and four peripheral collar cutouts to their final unmachined requirements. No separate VMC contour, pocket or flange-notch machining is added; supplier capability for these details must be verified against the released CAD.

The approximately 410 g finished mass places this part in ALM-FORG-002's mid-range class, not ALM-FORG-003's under-350 g class. Gross forging billet allowance includes flash and process losses and must not be interpreted as machining removal from the trimmed preform.

Near-net cleanup allowances follow ALM-FORG-002: light turned-feature stock and limited milled-feature stock, with no full-envelope roughing. Because the supplier removes detrimental skin before delivery, the generic minimum 1.5 mm first-cut instruction does not override the organizational light-cleanup route.

The two main machining stages are represented by two distinct lathe chuckings followed by one VMC clamping. Each lathe chucking contains facing and G71/G70 profile passes; journal and collar diameters remain separate sub-operations rather than being combined into a mixed-diameter cut.

Lathe facing is restricted to designated axial end surfaces and collar lands. Large die-formed radii and drafts are retained rather than recut, and the generic grooving step is omitted because F10 is supplied by the die.

Dedicated contour jaws, protective journal sleeves, suitable non-marking support and a positively clocked indexable VMC fixture are required. Fixture indexing changes access direction without unloading or releasing the part; gang/straddle tooling machines opposing flats where feasible.

VMC sub-operation 1 machines the left lug's opposing Y flats and establishes A; sub-operation 2 machines the right lug's Y flats. Sub-operations 3 and 4 machine the left and right Z face pairs respectively, with the left thickness taken from master CAD and F12 provisionally interpreted as the right lug thickness.

External flat machining precedes drilling. F04 is spotted and drilled to establish B before F01 is finished by slot milling relative to A-B; no extra left-lug hole is inferred from the aggregate lug description.

The left and right contact pads are provisionally flush with their adjacent lug faces, following the supplied graph assumptions. The two spotface sub-operations finish the positive-Z and negative-Z pad instances respectively, removing forging cleanup stock without creating an unsupported recess depth.

Saw cutting and parting are omitted for individual forged blanks. Lathe centre drilling is omitted because no centre-hole feature is specified and external support is used; axial boring, threading and knurling are omitted because corresponding features are absent.

Milling-template profile and pocket steps are unnecessary because those contours are die-formed. Spot drilling replaces centre drilling for F04; pilot and deep-hole drilling are unnecessary for the short clearance hole, and reaming, precision boring, tapping, countersinking and counterboring are omitted because their requirements are absent.
Finish milling uses climb cutting. General sharp-edge treatment is consolidated into the rapid bench deburr operations rather than represented as invented chamfer features.

Supplier penetrant inspection provides the pre-machining forging integrity gate. Magnetic-particle inspection is inapplicable to aluminium, and ultrasonic inspection is not added unless TM-2005 or the confirmed safety classification requires it.

Final inspection is a sampled shop-floor gauge gate, not a 100 percent CMM layout. A-B and C controls remain independent; listing all three datums at inspection does not establish a unified A-B-C hierarchy.

No coating, functional test, crush test or post-machining hardening is specified, so those conditional processes are omitted. Bench and inspection work follow the organizational rapid-production and sampling principles; cycle-time inputs remain for Pass 2.

Inspection, cleaning and general deburring have empty target lists because they do not produce separately identified graph features. Every non-body feature is physically formed by the supplier die or produced by its dedicated machining sub-operation.
